description: Primary EventHorizon protocol measurement view. Panels distinguish current state, finalized work, timing, duration, and reliability using the observation units defined in METRICS.md.

panels.title: Current activity by observation unit
panels.description: Producer-owned active gauges: `current_connected_clients`, `eventhorizon_coap_active_request_exchanges`, `eventhorizon_coap_active_con_response_exchanges`, and `eventhorizon_upnp_active_description_responses`. These current values use different observation units and are not summed. SSH is absent because Endlessh cannot observe peer closure and does not publish an active-client gauge.

panels.title: Telnet lifecycle accounting
panels.description: Tracked Telnet session lifecycle: `current_connected_clients{server="Telnet"}`, `eventhorizon_completed_sessions_total`, `eventhorizon_session_duration_ms_count`. **A session open at both edges of the selected range is counted in "Active now" and in neither of the other two**: its duration is not counted until it finishes. "Finalized" and "Duration observations" are expected to be equal; that is a reconciliation identity, not a coincidence. Counts accepted TCP connections, not unique people or devices.

panels.title: Telnet accepted vs. finalized
panels.description: Accepted tracked Telnet sessions and Telnet session finalizations: `total_connects{server="Telnet"}` and `eventhorizon_completed_sessions_total`. Accepted running above finished means sessions are being held open: that is the tarpit working, not a measurement error.

panels.title: Telnet accepted but not finalized
panels.description: Accepted minus finalized over the selected time range: `total_connects{server="Telnet"}` minus `eventhorizon_completed_sessions_total`. **A non-zero gap can be normal when connections or exchanges are still active. This panel is an operational hint, not deterministic validation proof.** Deterministic reconciliation requires settled boundary scrapes over a complete process epoch; see `METRICS.md`.

panels.title: Telnet finalizations by reason
panels.description: Telnet session finalization reason: `eventhorizon_completed_sessions_total{disconnect_reason}`, five bounded values. "Finalized" does not mean a login, command, or Telnet negotiation completed successfully, and ordinary inactivity is not itself a finalization reason. **This panel counts finalized sessions only.** This counter uses bounded labels only: no errno, no error text, no identities.

panels.title: Telnet interaction depth at finalization
panels.description: Telnet interaction depth: `eventhorizon_session_interaction_depth_total{depth_level}`. A bounded final classification of the furthest meaningful application interaction reached: `0` none, `1` incomplete input, `2` exactly one complete non-empty line, `3` meaningful continuation after that line. It is not a command count, a line count, or attacker sophistication. **This panel counts finalized sessions only.**

panels.title: Telnet session duration distribution
panels.description: Telnet session duration: `eventhorizon_session_duration_ms`. Monotonic elapsed time from acceptance to the one finalization boundary, observed by the server. It includes time before the first server write. **This panel counts finalized observations only; open sessions are absent.** Not a configured delay, not an active-session age, not a client-perceived latency.

panels.title: Telnet session duration (mean / p50 / p95)
panels.description: Telnet session duration: `eventhorizon_session_duration_ms`. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: Telnet time to first server write (p50 / p95)
panels.description: First-write delay: `eventhorizon_telnet_first_write_delay_ms`. Monotonic elapsed time from an accepted connection to its first successful positive-byte server write. **This is measured server-side timing, not the configured delay.** It is not first-response latency and not time to client receipt. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: Telnet time between server writes (p50 / p95)
panels.description: Inter-write interval: `eventhorizon_telnet_inter_write_interval_ms`. Monotonic elapsed time between consecutive successful positive-byte server writes. **Measured, not configured**; not a response latency and not a round-trip time. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: Telnet read and write errors by reason
panels.description: `eventhorizon_read_errors_total` and `eventhorizon_write_errors_total`, four bounded reasons: `timeout`, `reset`, `closed`, `other`. A clean TCP EOF is a peer finalization, not an error, and a positive partial write is byte evidence rather than an error. Zero errors does not prove telemetry completeness. This counter uses bounded labels only: no errno, no error text, no identities.

panels.title: Telnet application bytes
panels.description: Positive socket-return bytes only: `eventhorizon_bytes_received_total`, `eventhorizon_bytes_sent_total`. Includes protocol framing, incomplete input, and partial writes; excludes EOF, failed, retryable, and zero-byte I/O. **This is not TCP/IP wire volume and does not prove client receipt.** Container network bytes are the authoritative volume evidence and live in the optional Defender Cost row.

panels.title: MQTT Network Connection lifecycle accounting
panels.description: **These are MQTT Network Connections, not MQTT Sessions.** A tracked MQTT Network Connection is one accepted TCP connection, whether or not it ever reaches an accepted CONNECT; an MQTT Session is a protocol concept that can outlive and resume across network connections and is never measured here. Sources: `current_connected_clients{server="MQTT"}`, `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_finalizations_total`, `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_duration_ms_count`. **A connection open at both edges of the selected range is counted in "Active now" and in neither of the other two.** "Finalized" and "Duration observations" are expected to be equal.

panels.title: MQTT accepted vs. finalized
panels.description: Accepted tracked MQTT Network Connections and their finalizations: `total_connects{server="MQTT"}` and `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_finalizations_total`. Accepted counts TCP acceptance, not accepted CONNECT.

panels.title: MQTT accepted but not finalized
panels.description: Accepted minus finalized over the selected time range. **A non-zero gap can be normal when connections or exchanges are still active. This panel is an operational hint, not deterministic validation proof.** Deterministic reconciliation requires settled boundary scrapes over a complete process epoch; see `METRICS.md`.

panels.title: MQTT finalizations by reason
panels.description: MQTT Network Connection finalization reason: `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_finalizations_total{finalization_reason}`, ten bounded values. The first authoritative terminal reason is retained even if later cleanup encounters another failure. It finalizes a transport connection, not persistent MQTT Session State. **This panel counts finalized observations only.**

panels.title: MQTT interaction depth at finalization
panels.description: MQTT interaction depth: `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_interaction_depth_total{depth_level}`. Bounded final classification: `0` no accepted CONNECT, `1` accepted CONNECT without a meaningful operation, `2` one accepted PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE, `3` at least two. Control packets, acknowledgements, keep-alive traffic, malformed packets, and retransmissions do not increase depth. It is not a packet count, topic count, or QoS depth.

panels.title: MQTT Network Connection duration distribution
panels.description: MQTT Network Connection duration: `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_duration_ms`. Acceptance to the one finalization boundary, including time before an accepted CONNECT. **Counts finalized observations only; open connections are absent.** This is not an MQTT Session duration and not a CONNECT exchange duration.

panels.title: MQTT Network Connection duration (mean / p50 / p95)
panels.description: MQTT Network Connection duration: `eventhorizon_mqtt_network_connection_duration_ms`. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: MQTT CONNECT-to-CONNACK time (p50 / p95)
panels.description: MQTT CONNECT-to-CONNACK duration: `eventhorizon_mqtt_connect_to_connack_duration_ms`. From an accepted MQTT 3.1.1 CONNECT to complete successful transmission of its success CONNACK. Excludes pre-CONNECT connection time and all later activity. **Server-observed: it does not prove the client received or parsed the CONNACK**, and it is not a round-trip or client response time. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: MQTT protocol actions
panels.description: `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="mqtt"}`, twelve bounded actions. Scoped to MQTT deliberately: a family-wide sum across protocols mixes unrelated observation boundaries and has no useful meaning. Counts server-side boundaries crossed, not client receipt, parsing, or engagement. A partial MQTT Control Packet write emits no completed-packet action.

panels.title: MQTT read and write errors by reason
panels.description: `eventhorizon_read_errors_total` and `eventhorizon_write_errors_total` for MQTT, four bounded reasons. A clean TCP EOF is a peer finalization, not an error. Zero errors does not prove telemetry completeness. This counter uses bounded labels only: no errno, no error text, no identities.

panels.title: MQTT application bytes
panels.description: Positive socket-return bytes only: `eventhorizon_bytes_received_total`, `eventhorizon_bytes_sent_total`. Includes protocol framing and partial writes. **Not TCP/IP wire volume; does not prove client receipt.**

panels.title: CoAP request exchange lifecycle accounting
panels.description: Active CoAP request exchange: `eventhorizon_coap_active_request_exchanges`; finalizations from `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="coap"}`; observations from `eventhorizon_coap_request_exchange_duration_ms_count`. An active request exchange is an accepted supported GET with neither a transmitted matching response nor a termination: it is an outstanding **request obligation**, not a connected client and not a UDP session. **A request still open at both edges of the selected range is counted in "Active now" only.**

panels.title: CoAP request handling time (p50 / p95 by outcome)
panels.description: CoAP request-exchange duration: `eventhorizon_coap_request_exchange_duration_ms{outcome}`. From acceptance of the first non-duplicate supported GET until either the first matching response is transmitted (`response_sent`) or the exchange is terminated (`terminated`). It excludes duplicates, response retransmissions, and **all later Acknowledgement waiting**: that time belongs to the CoAP reliability panels below. Not a CoAP session duration. `response_sent` proves server-side transmission, not client receipt. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: CoAP request outcomes
panels.description: `eventhorizon_coap_request_exchange_duration_ms_count{outcome}`. Shows **when** request exchanges reached a terminal boundary. Two mutually exclusive outcomes: `response_sent` and `terminated`.

panels.title: CoAP CON reliability lifecycle accounting
panels.description: Active CoAP CON-response exchange: `eventhorizon_coap_active_con_response_exchanges`; finalizations from `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="coap"}`; observations from `eventhorizon_coap_con_response_exchange_duration_ms_count`. A successfully transmitted outbound Confirmable response still awaiting a matching Acknowledgement or Reset and not yet retry-exhausted. It is an outstanding **message-layer obligation**, independent from the request exchange above and not an active endpoint. Retransmissions are non-terminal and never finalize it; duplicate and late control messages create no second outcome.

panels.title: CoAP reliability waiting time (p50 / p95 by outcome)
panels.description: CoAP CON-response exchange duration: `eventhorizon_coap_con_response_exchange_duration_ms{outcome}`. From the first successful outbound Confirmable response transmission until the first matching Acknowledgement, first matching Reset, or retry exhaustion. **Includes retransmission waiting** and excludes all request-exchange time before the response was sent. Three bounded outcomes: `ack_received`, `rst_received`, `retry_exhausted`. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: CoAP CON reliability outcomes
panels.description: `eventhorizon_coap_con_response_exchange_duration_ms_count{outcome}`. Shows **when** outbound Confirmable response exchanges reached a terminal boundary.

panels.title: CoAP protocol actions
panels.description: `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="coap"}`, eight bounded actions. Request actions are Token-correlated; CON-response reliability actions are Message-ID-correlated: the two populations are independent. A sent or retransmitted action requires `sendto()` to return the exact encoded datagram length. Scoped to CoAP deliberately: a family-wide sum across protocols has no useful meaning.

panels.title: CoAP write errors by reason
panels.description: `eventhorizon_write_errors_total{protocol="coap"}`, four bounded reasons. A short positive UDP send emits no sent action and is recorded here with reason `other`. Receive failures and malformed datagrams precede the supported-request boundary and are not counted here. This counter uses bounded labels only: no errno, no error text, no identities.

panels.title: UPnP SSDP discovery actions
panels.description: `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="upnp"}` restricted to the SSDP discovery exchange. Discovery and device-description are **independent** exchanges in this implementation: this dashboard does not correlate an M-SEARCH with a later description GET, and the ratio between these two bars establishes no discovery follow-through. A sent action proves server-side transmission, not client receipt.

panels.title: UPnP device-description actions
panels.description: `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="upnp"}` restricted to the HTTP device-description exchange: `description_get_received`, `description_response_started`, `description_response_completed`, `description_response_terminated`. A valid GET that never produces a positive-byte write is a pre-start failure: it never starts a response and therefore never terminates one.

panels.title: UPnP description response lifecycle accounting
panels.description: Active description response: `eventhorizon_upnp_active_description_responses`; finalizations from `eventhorizon_protocol_actions_total{protocol="upnp"}`; observations from `eventhorizon_upnp_description_stream_duration_ms_count`. **UPnP description responses still active**: started by a first positive-byte write but not yet completed or terminated: are counted in "Active now" and contribute no duration. Its current count is an independently observed response-state measurement, not a connected-client count and not derived from the action counters.

panels.title: UPnP description response time (p50 / p95 by outcome)
panels.description: Description stream duration: `eventhorizon_upnp_description_stream_duration_ms{outcome}`. From description response start (first positive-byte write) to its one completion or termination outcome. `completed` requires complete HTTP/1.1 headers and exactly the declared `Content-Length` bytes of a valid `Content-Type: text/xml` description written within 30 seconds. **This duration is observed by the server. It does not prove the client received the response.** Not a request-to-response latency and not an active response age. Computed over the selected time range from finalized observations only. Blank means nothing finished in range: it does not mean nothing is happening; check "Active now".

panels.title: UPnP description response outcomes
panels.description: `eventhorizon_upnp_description_stream_duration_ms_count{outcome}`. Shows **when** description responses reached a terminal boundary. Two mutually exclusive outcomes: `completed` and `terminated`.

panels.title: UPnP write errors by reason
panels.description: `eventhorizon_write_errors_total{protocol="upnp"}`, four bounded reasons. Covers write failures crossing the frozen UPnP reliability boundaries, including SSDP discovery responses and description-response writes. This counter uses bounded labels only: no errno, no error text, no identities.

panels.title: Rejected metric datagrams by reason
panels.description: `eventhorizon_exporter_malformed_messages_total{reason}` counts datagrams rejected before metric mutation. Labels are bounded and contain no errno, error text, or identity. Zero does not prove delivery completeness: lost datagrams are invisible, valid duplicates can be applied again, and exporter restart resets in-memory state.

panels.title: Rejected metric datagrams in range
panels.description: `eventhorizon_exporter_malformed_messages_total` summed over the selected range. Zero means the exporter rejected no observed datagram. It does not prove that every producer event arrived or that no valid datagram was duplicated.

panels.title: Accepted SSH connections
panels.description: Accepted SSH TCP connections from `total_connects{server="SSH"}`. A successful `accept()` is exact. SSH has no active-client gauge because Endlessh does not read client sockets and cannot observe when a peer has gone.

panels.title: Right-censored at server shutdown
panels.description: Tracked-client observations that ended because the server stopped while the client was still tracked: `eventhorizon_ssh_tracked_client_lifetime_ms_count{observation_end_reason="server_shutdown"}`. The observation ended for a server-side reason, so the tracked-client lifetime is at least the recorded value and its true extent is unknown. These are excluded from the lifetime distribution beside this panel.

panels.title: Tracked-client lifetime: write failures
panels.description: Observed lifetime of Endlessh-tracked SSH clients: `eventhorizon_ssh_tracked_client_lifetime_ms{observation_end_reason="write_failed"}`. From accepted TCP connection until a scheduled write failed and Endlessh removed the tracked client. **This is not peer connection duration:** peer EOF is not directly observed, the recorded value does not identify the exact peer-disconnect time or necessarily its cause, and detection may occur multiple write intervals later. Right-censored `server_shutdown` observations are excluded.
Optional container resource evidence. Requires the `docker-compose.cost.yml` overlay and its cAdvisor metrics; normal EventHorizon deployment does not require cAdvisor.
CPU time consumed by each tarpit container, derived from cumulative cAdvisor CPU seconds. The value is a percentage of one CPU core and is not normalized by machine cores or container limits.
panels.title: Tarpit CPU usage (% of one core)

panels.description: Receive and transmit rates from each tarpit container interface as observed by cAdvisor. Values include protocol, transport, and network overhead.
panels.title: Tarpit container network RX/TX
